From f025a2b8d93358467b8e8f4b3a617e88c5f02fab Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Sunil Khatri <sunil.khatri@amd.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 12:09:05 +0530
Subject: [PATCH] drm/amdgpu: clean up the amdgpu_cs_parser_bos
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

In low memory conditions, kmalloc can fail. In such conditions
unlock the mutex for a clean exit.

We do not need to amdgpu_bo_list_put as it's been handled in the
amdgpu_cs_parser_fini.

Fixes: 737da5363cc0 ("drm/amdgpu: update the functions to use amdgpu version of hmm")
Reported-by: kernel test robot <lkp@intel.com>
Reported-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@linaro.org>
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/r/202602030017.7E0xShmH-lkp@intel.com/
Signed-off-by: Sunil Khatri <sunil.khatri@amd.com>
Reviewed-by: Christian König <christian.koenig@amd.com>
Signed-off-by: Alex Deucher <alexander.deucher@amd.com>

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_cs.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_cs.c
index d591dce0f3b3..f3b5bcdbf2ae 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_cs.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_cs.c
@@ -892,8 +892,10 @@ static int amdgpu_cs_parser_bos(struct amdgpu_cs_parser *p,
 		struct amdgpu_bo *bo = e->bo;
 
 		e->range = amdgpu_hmm_range_alloc(NULL);
-		if (unlikely(!e->range))
-			return -ENOMEM;
+		if (unlikely(!e->range)) {
+			r = -ENOMEM;
+			goto out_free_user_pages;
+		}
 
 		r = amdgpu_ttm_tt_get_user_pages(bo, e->range);
 		if (r)
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### Modifications per file

**File: `drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_cs.c`**

- In function `amdgpu_cs_parser_bos`, within the loop processing user pages:
  - **Before**: When `amdgpu_hmm_range_alloc()` returns `NULL`, the code directly returned `-ENOMEM` without performing any cleanup.
  - **After**: The failure sets error code `r = -ENOMEM` and then jumps to label `out_free_user_pages`. This ensures proper cleanup (freeing allocated user pages, unlocking mutexes, etc.) before returning.

### Relationship between modifications

The single change addresses a resource leak and improper error handling under low memory conditions. Previously, a failed memory allocation (`amdgpu_hmm_range_alloc` returns `NULL`) caused an immediate return, skipping the cleanup steps that are normally performed for other errors in the same block. By redirecting to the existing `out_free_user_pages` label, the fix ensures that all necessary unwinding (including freeing already‑allocated resources and releasing the mutex) occurs, leading to a clean exit. The patch also notes that the explicit `amdgpu_bo_list_put` is unnecessary because it is already handled in `amdgpu_cs_parser_fini`.
